baslik: How Did Mehmed II Lock the Bosphorus in Just 139 Days? 🏰 (1452) #shorts
aciklama:
With over 40,000 vessels passing through every year, the Bosphorus Strait remains the ultimate key to the Black Sea. Yet 574 years ago, in 1452, this narrow 660-meter waterway was locked down in just 139 days.

To cut off Black Sea supply lines to Constantinople, 20-year-old Sultan Mehmed II built Rumeli Fortress ('Bogazkesen' — Strait-Cutter) in 139 days. In November 1452, its giant bronze bombards sank Captain Antonio Rizzo's Venetian ship—sealing the strait 6 months before the fall of Constantinople.
